shortDescription: Lockheed Martin NYSE:LMT on Friday unveiled its new PAC-3 Edge missile interceptor, which it said will will add "a revolutionary defensive capability" against hypersonic and advanced missile threats, as the U.S. military seeks to strengthen its capabilities to counter emerging aerial threats.Lockhe…

said PAC-3 Edge incorporates a new seeker, upgraded flight controls, and a ​multi-pulse rocket motor supplied by Northrop Grumman

, enhancing ​the interceptor's ability to counter advanced threats, including hypersonic missiles, ‌and providing greater speed and maneuverability, allowing it to fly at higher altitudes and longer distances than other PAC-3 missiles.
The new interceptor is part of the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor program currently in competition, and builds on Lockheed's
PAC-3 MSE, which has been used extensively to defend against missile attacks in Ukraine and Iran.
"The cost of this would be about that of the existing PAC-3 MSE," Tim Cahill, Lockheed
president of missiles and ​fire control Tim Cahill ⁠told Reuters. "At full production, the annual rate would be about 2,000 ​units a year, comparable with PAC-3 MSE."
said it will advance development and begin testing PAC-3 Edge in 2027 to prepare for rapid deployment by 2031.
